id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

from.description:
The From address to be used in the email. If a Member is given, instead of a string, it will use the email
address for the Member record.

to.description:
The list of To addresses to be used in the email. If a Member is given, instead of a string, it will use the email
address for the Member record.

cc.description:
The list of CC addresses to be used in the email. If a Member is given, instead of a string, it will use the email
address for the Member record.

bcc.description:
The list of BCC addresses to be used in the email. If a Member is given, instead of a string, it will use the email
address for the Member record.

subject.description: The subject line of the email

content.description: The body of the email. It may be plain text or html, as specified in the content_type.

vars.description:
This Template DOES NOT use {@link Template}. {@link Template} uses FreeMarker for templates. This is literal string
substitution.

As template variables to specify the fields on the subject and content.

Example: In the content/subject template, `Hi it is nice to meet you $USER at $PLACE.`
with vars passed as `{"USER": "c3User", "PLACE": "1400SeaPort"}`  =>  `Hi it is nice to meet you c3User at 1400Seaport.`

content_type.description: The content type of the email, default is 'text/plain' if not specified.

contentType.description: The content type of the email, default is 'text/plain' if not specified.

attachment.description:
A single attachment that may be sent with the email.
It should be created before the Mail record.

attachments.description: Attach one or more files in an email. Supported by only certain {@link MailConfig.serviceProvider}s.

title:
For sending email messages from code. This is not intended for marketing or mass emails,
but for notifications that are generated in response to actions or thresholds.

The Mail record should be upserted before sending the email.
The email sent is recorded in the server logs, so may be searched in Splunk.
name: Mail
